workload.description: One HTTP request an app hands to test-cap. Each function names what its n counts instead (cookies on a request, key-ring entries, policy requirements, public paths, stored records, password characters), because the cost of an authentication request grows with those, not with a batch size. 640 is a busy minute of sign-in traffic for one of the owner's apps.

createAuth.config.store: fixed: the memory store, so the figure is test-cap's own work and no database's
createAuth.config.hibpFetch: fixed: answers from memory with a padding row, so no request leaves the process
createAuth.config.policy: fixed: absent, so every requirement is the default AAL2
createAuth.config.random: fixed: absent, the system random source
createAuth.config.sendEmail: fixed: keeps each message in memory; sending is the app's own cost
createAuth.config.onEvent: fixed: absent; a sink is the app's own cost and cannot change an outcome
createAuth.config.trustedProxies: fixed: absent; phase 3 reads no forwarded header
createAuth.config.argon2Cost: fixed: the reduced test-mode cost; the sign-in benchmark's variant measures the real one

defineAuthPolicy.input.version: fixed: one short label, which is only stored
defineAuthPolicy.input.trust: not covered: OIDC trust arrives in phase 5
